# Broadside primitives

<!-- Generated by scripts/primitives.mjs (npm run docs) from the registries. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every building block a battle in `src/config/battles.js` can use. How to combine them, and how to add new
ones: [EXTENDING.md](EXTENDING.md).

- [Goals](#goals): `sink`, `boss`, `capture`, `treasure`, `escort`, `hold`, `breakthrough`, `timer`, `waves`, `protect`, `hunt`, `reach`, `survive`

- [Event actions](#event-actions-do): `spawn`, `banner`, `wind`, `fog`, `say`, `retreat`, `reveal`, `heal`

- [Hats](#hats): `cabin`, `rojo`, `comodoro`, `oro`, `kate`, `morion`, `armada`

- [Land and landmarks](#land-and-landmarks): `town`, `harbour`, `lighthouse`, `peak`, `volcano`, `church`, `windmill`, `ruin`, `castle`, `skull`, `wreck`, `stacks`, `mangroves`

## Goals

A battle lists `goals: [{ kind, ...params }]` (all must be met) or the shorthand `goal: 'boss'`; with
neither it is `sink`. Params marked optional (their description says "default") may be left out.

### `sink`

Sink every enemy ship.

No params.

### `boss`

Sink the ship carrying boss: { captain, title, hat }; wins that captain's hat.

No params.

Hooks: `failed`, `hud`.

Can be lost: `escaped`.

### `capture`

Take every enemy fort: shoot it silent, then land troops.

No params.

Hooks: `failed`, `hud`.

Can be lost: `marines`.

### `treasure`

Haul up floating chests by sailing over them; salvors carry chests until sunk or boarded.

| param | description |
|---|---|
| `need` | chests to haul up |
| `chests` | chest positions [{ x, y }] (portrait fractions) |

Hooks: `setup`, `update`, `failed`, `hud`, `sunk`, `steer`, `tip` ("chest").

Can be lost: `treasure`.

### `escort`

Bring merchantmen out through the exit at the top of the chart.

| param | description |
|---|---|
| `need` | how many must get through |
| `ships` | the merchantmen (ship defs); they sail themselves |

Hooks: `setup`, `failed`, `hud`, `escaped`, `weigh`, `tip` ("exit").

Can be lost: `escort`.

### `hold`

Hold your forts (team: 'player') until the clock runs out.

| param | description |
|---|---|
| `secs` | seconds to hold |
| `grace` | seconds to retake a silenced fort (default 18) |

Hooks: `setup`, `update`, `failed`, `hud`, `aiForts` (true).

Can be lost: `fort`.

### `breakthrough`

Get the flagship out through the exit at the top of the chart.

| param | description |
|---|---|
| `ship` | which of your ships is the flagship (default 0, the first) |

Hooks: `setup`, `failed`, `hud`, `escaped`, `weigh`, `tip` ("exit").

Can be lost: `flagship`.

### `timer`

Meet the battle's other goals before time runs out.

| param | description |
|---|---|
| `secs` | seconds allowed |

Hooks: `failed`, `hud`.

Can be lost: `time`.

### `waves`

Endless Skirmish: wave after wave; never won, ends when the fleet is gone.

No params.

Hooks: `setup`, `update`, `hud`, `endless` (true).

### `protect`

Keep named ships afloat and named forts firing; lose any one and the battle is lost.

| param | description |
|---|---|
| `ships` | names of English ships to keep afloat (a number is your fleet's nth ship, 0 = the first) |
| `allies` | ship defs added as allied captains who sail and fight on their own (also guarded) |
| `forts` | names of your forts that must keep firing |
| `secs` | optional: seconds to keep them safe, after which this goal is met (without it, pair with another goal) |

Hooks: `setup`, `failed`, `hud`, `weigh`, `aiForts`, `tip` ("protect").

Can be lost: `lost`.

### `hunt`

Sink (or take) the named enemy ships before they get away; the rest are optional.

| param | description |
|---|---|
| `ships` | names of the enemy ships to sink (a name or a list) |

Hooks: `failed`, `hud`, `tip` ("hunt").

Can be lost: `escaped`.

### `reach`

Bring a ship (or the named one) into a ring marked on the chart, and hold it there if secs is given.

| param | description |
|---|---|
| `x` | centre across the chart (portrait fraction) |
| `y` | centre down the chart (portrait fraction) |
| `r` | radius as a fraction of the chart's width (default 0.1) |
| `ship` | optional: the name of the English ship that must get there |
| `secs` | optional: seconds a ship must stay inside |
| `label` | the marker's caption (default "Sail here") |

Hooks: `setup`, `update`, `failed`, `hud`, `tip` ("reach").

Can be lost: `ship`.

### `survive`

Keep the fleet afloat until the clock runs out; the enemy needn't be beaten.

| param | description |
|---|---|
| `secs` | seconds to hold out |

Hooks: `hud`.

## Abilities

A ship type (`abilities` in TYPES) or one ship in a battle (`abilities` on its def) carries
`{ abilityId: config | true }`; `true` takes the defaults, and a battle ship's config is merged over its type's.

### `mortar`

Lobs shells over islands onto a spot; the HUD rings where they land.

| param | default | description |
|---|---|---|
| `range` | `430` | max range |
| `reload` | `6.5` | seconds between shells |
| `dmg` | `22` | damage at the centre |
| `radius` | `36` | burst radius |

Hooks: `init`, `update`.

Ship types that carry it: `bomb`.

### `fireship`

Steers for the nearest enemy and explodes alongside; any sinking sets off a blast.

| param | default | description |
|---|---|---|
| `dmg` | `45` | ramming damage |
| `splash` | `18` | blast damage at the centre |
| `radius` | `70` | blast radius |

Hooks: `init`, `update`, `steer`, `sunk`.

Ship types that carry it: `fireship`.

### `launcher`

Puts another ship over the side every so often (fireships by default).

| param | default | description |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | `fireship` | ship type to launch |
| `name` | `Fireship` | their name |
| `every` | `16` | seconds between launches |
| `max` | `3` | most afloat at once |
| `range` | `520` | only while an enemy is this close |
| `banner` | `["Fireship!","Sink her before she reaches you"]` | [title, subtitle] shown on launch, or null |

Hooks: `init`, `update`.

### `mineLayer`

Drops a mine astern while an enemy is near.

| param | default | description |
|---|---|---|
| `every` | `8` | seconds between mines |
| `range` | `300` | how near an enemy must be |

Hooks: `init`, `update`.

### `oars`

Rowed: keeps moving whatever the wind.

| param | default | description |
|---|---|---|
| `min` | `0.86` | lowest wind speed factor |

Hooks: `init`, `wind`.

Ship types that carry it: `xebec`.

### `repair`

Carpenters patch the hull: slowly once out of action, or always at a low rate.

| param | default | description |
|---|---|---|
| `rate` | `2` | hull a second once out of action |
| `idle` | `5` | seconds out of gun range and unhit before the carpenters start |
| `always` | `0` | hull a second at all times, even in action |
| `max` | `1` | share of full hull they can patch back up to (0-1) |

Hooks: `init`, `update`.

### `ram`

Reinforced bow: sailing into an enemy ship stoves in her hull and slows both.

| param | default | description |
|---|---|---|
| `dmg` | `26` | damage at full speed |
| `slow` | `4` | seconds the rammed ship is slowed |
| `every` | `3` | seconds between rams |
| `charge` | `260` | AI rammers charge a foe this close |

Hooks: `init`, `update`, `steer`.

### `flee`

Breaks off and runs for the nearest edge of the chart once badly hurt; reaching it, she escapes.

| param | default | description |
|---|---|---|
| `below` | `0.5` | hull share (0-1) at which she runs |
| `speed` | `1.15` | her speed while running, times normal |
| `say` | `She’s making a run for it!` | what she calls as she runs, or null |

Hooks: `update`, `wind`.

### `rally`

Friendly ships near her reload faster.

| param | default | description |
|---|---|---|
| `radius` | `180` | how near friends must be |
| `reload` | `0.7` | their reload time, times normal (0.7 = 30% faster) |

Hooks: `update`.

## Event conditions (WHEN)

`events: [{ ...conditions, ...actions }]`: an event fires once, the first tick all of its conditions
hold (no conditions: at the start), and runs its actions in order.

| key | fires when |
|---|---|
| `at` | seconds into the battle |
| `enemiesLeft` | at most this many enemy ships afloat |
| `bossHp` | the boss hull at or below this share (0-1) |
| `fortsHeld` | you hold at least this many forts |
| `shipSunk` | the named ship (or every ship in a list) has gone down |
| `shipNear` | { name?, x, y, r }: an English ship (or the named ship, either side) within r of the spot |
| `goalDone` | the goal at this index in goals is met |

## Event actions (DO)

| key | does |
|---|---|
| `spawn` | ship defs to add (enemy unless team: 'player') |
| `banner` | [title, subtitle] across the screen |
| `wind` | the wind backs round to blow toward this heading (degrees) |
| `fog` | fog rolls in to this sight distance (0 lifts it) |
| `say` | [ship name, text]: a line spoken over that ship |
| `retreat` | the named enemy ships (true: every enemy ship) break off and run for the edge of the chart |
| `reveal` | the fog lifts and every ship shows for this many seconds (true: the fog clears for good) |
| `heal` | every English ship afloat patches this share (0-1) of her full hull |

## Ship types

From `TYPES` in `src/config/ships.js`. Speed in units/sec, turn in rad/sec, reload in sec; L × B is
length × beam. Enemy hulls are multiplied by the battle's `ai.hpMul` unless the ship sets `hp`.

| type | label | hp | guns | reload | speed | turn | range | marines | masts | L × B | rig | abilities |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sloop` | Sloop | 70 | 3 | 2.4 | 62 | 1.35 | 235 | 10 | 2 | 60 × 22 | square |  |
| `brig` | Brig | 85 | 3 | 2.6 | 57 | 1.15 | 240 | 15 | 2 | 66 × 24 | square |  |
| `frigate` | Frigate | 130 | 5 | 3 | 50 | 0.85 | 255 | 20 | 3 | 84 × 30 | square |  |
| `manowar` | Man-o'-war | 210 | 7 | 3.3 | 43 | 0.62 | 280 | 30 | 3 | 104 × 38 | square |  |
| `galleon` | Galleon | 150 | 6 | 3.4 | 42 | 0.65 | 270 | 20 | 3 | 92 × 34 | square |  |
| `schooner` | Schooner | 60 | 2 | 2.2 | 70 | 1.5 | 220 | 12 | 2 | 56 × 18 | fore-aft |  |
| `xebec` | Xebec | 75 | 3 | 2.5 | 58 | 1.4 | 230 | 18 | 3 | 62 × 18 | lateen | oars |
| `bomb` | Bomb ketch | 95 | 2 | 3 | 44 | 0.9 | 220 | 10 | 2 | 64 × 24 | square | mortar {"range":430,"reload":6.5,"dmg":22,"radius":36} |
| `fireship` | Fireship | 40 | 0 | 9 | 62 | 1.25 | 0 | 0 | 2 | 54 × 20 | square | fireship |

Other flags: `merchant`: `merchant` = `true`.

| hat | name | from |

| `cabin` | Cabin boy's cap | Finish the Shakedown Cruise |
| `rojo` | Red tricorne | Capitán Rojo of La Bruja |
| `comodoro` | Commodore's bicorne | El Comodoro of San Cristóbal |
| `oro` | Admiral's plumed hat | Almirante de Oro of the Santísima Trinidad |
| `kate` | Calico Kate's skull hat | Calico Kate of the Black Wyvern |
| `morion` | Iron morion | Marqués de Hierro of the San Jerónimo |
| `armada` | Captain-General's crown hat | The Capitán General of the Real Felipe |

## Geography and openings

Battle fields from `TERRAIN` in `src/sim/terrain.js`. Positions are portrait fractions and radii map
units, as for islands; landscape turns the whole layout (coasts and long axes included). Ships may not start on
land, on a reef, or (if they are big enough to ground) on a shoal; `npm run check` says so.

### `islands`

Land. Ships sail round it and shot can’t pass it; a fort stands on one. A stretched island is a long ridge, collided and steered round as drawn.

| field | description |
|---|---|
| `x` | centre across the chart (portrait fraction) |
| `y` | centre down the chart (portrait fraction) |
| `r` | radius in map units (half the width of a long one) |
| `stretch` | optional: length over width, 1 = round (default 1) |
| `angle` | optional: direction of the long axis in degrees, 0 = across the chart, 90 = down it (default 0) |

### `shoals`

Shallow, pale water. Ships longer than 64 (brigs and up) run aground: they crawl at 30% speed and 60% helm, lose 4 hull as they strike and 1 a second while they grind on. Sloops, schooners, xebecs, bomb ketches and fireships sail over. Captains and drawn courses steer big ships round them.

| field | description |
|---|---|
| `x` | centre across the chart (portrait fraction) |
| `y` | centre down the chart (portrait fraction) |
| `r` | radius in map units (half the width of a long one) |
| `stretch` | optional: length over width, 1 = round (default 1) |
| `angle` | optional: direction of the long axis in degrees, 0 = across the chart, 90 = down it (default 0) |

### `reefs`

Rocks just under the surf. Any ship crossing one loses up to 16 hull a second and is slowed to 50%. Captains and drawn courses steer round them. Long thin ones (stretch 3-6) make reef lines.

| field | description |
|---|---|
| `x` | centre across the chart (portrait fraction) |
| `y` | centre down the chart (portrait fraction) |
| `r` | radius in map units (half the width of a long one) |
| `stretch` | optional: length over width, 1 = round (default 1) |
| `angle` | optional: direction of the long axis in degrees, 0 = across the chart, 90 = down it (default 0) |

### `coast`

A land mass along one edge of the chart with a ragged shore, coves and capes. Ships collide with it like an island and steer along it. One object, or a list for several coasts (a strait).

| field | description |
|---|---|
| `side` | which edge: 'left', 'right', 'top' or 'bottom' (of the portrait chart; landscape turns it with everything else) |
| `depth` | how far the land reaches in, as a fraction of the chart across that edge (0.1-0.3 is typical) |
| `rough` | optional: how ragged the shore is, 0 = smooth (default 0.3) |
| `coves` | optional: bays cut into the land, [{ at, width, depth }] (fractions: where along the edge, how wide, how deep) |
| `capes` | optional: headlands pushed out to sea, [{ at, width, depth }] |
| `seed` | optional: a number that reshapes the shore (default from side and depth) |

### `fleetAt`

Where your campaign fleet starts: bottom (the default), top (facing down the chart), left, right, center, or explicit { slots: [[x, y], ...], h } with one slot per ship in fleet order. Pair it with enemy positions anywhere for ambushes and enemies astern.

| value | description |
|---|---|
| `fleetAt` | 'bottom' \| 'top' \| 'left' \| 'right' \| 'center' \| { slots: [[x, y], ...] (portrait fractions, up to 5), h (heading in degrees; default -90) } |

Example: a narrow channel between a coast and a long island, with shoals off the cape.

```js
coast: { side: 'left', depth: 0.2, capes: [{ at: 0.45, width: 0.3, depth: 0.1 }] },
islands: [{ x: 0.72, y: 0.46, r: 34, stretch: 2.6, angle: 80 }],
shoals: [{ x: 0.42, y: 0.3, r: 34, stretch: 1.6, angle: 20 }],
reefs: [{ x: 0.55, y: 0.66, r: 12, stretch: 4, angle: -10 }], fleetAt: 'left',
```

## Land and landmarks

The look of a battle's land and what stands on it: `src/config/lands.js`, keyed by battle id (or a battle def's own
`land`), with landmark kinds from `LANDMARKS` in `src/sim/land.js`. Most are scenery; harbour (repairs), town (loot),
peak and volcano (a lee that steals the wind) and lighthouse (sight in fog) change the battle. `npm run check`
checks that each one fits on its land, inside the outline ships collide with.

| field | description |
|---|---|
| `style` | optional: the look of the land: port, windward, main, golden, pirate, campeche, armada (default: the battle's region) |
| `relief` | optional: per-island shape, [{ island, height, cliffs, at }]: island = island index; height = optional: hill height multiplier (default 1); cliffs = optional: share of the shore that is cliff, 0-1 (default the style's); at = optional: which side the cliffs face, degrees (default random) |
| `landmarks` | optional: a list of landmarks, { kind, ...placement, ...params } |

Every landmark is `{ kind, ...placement, ...params }`. Placement (one of island, coast, or x and y):

| field | description |
|---|---|
| `island` | island index it stands on (or use coast, or x and y) |
| `coast` | coast index it stands on (0 for a single coast) |
| `x` | optional: across the chart (portrait fraction), for a landmark in the water |
| `y` | optional: down the chart (portrait fraction) |
| `at` | optional: on an island, degrees from its centre (0 = east, 90 = down the chart; default 90); on a coast, how far along its edge (0-1; default 0.5) |
| `d` | optional: on an island, how far out from the centre toward the shore (0-1; default 0) |
| `inland` | optional: on a coast, map units in from the shore (default 50) |

### `town`

Houses round a square in the region’s style: English timber and brick, Spanish whitewash and terracotta, a pirate shanty on stilts, a fishing village of palm-thatched huts or a pastel harbour city. Chimneys smoke and a flag flies. Given loot, an enemy town can be bombarded: shot that lands on it sets it burning, and once it is ruined its loot is yours (prize gold, paid if you win).

| param | default | description |
|---|---|---|
| `houses` | `6` | optional: how many buildings (default 6) |
| `look` | (the region’s) | optional: english, spanish, shanty, village, city (default: the region's) |
| `name` | `the town` | optional: what the banner calls it (default "the town") |
| `loot` | `0` | optional: prize gold for sacking it, 0 = scenery only (default 0) |
| `hp` | `60` | optional: how much shot it takes to sack (default 60, about fifteen balls) |
| `team` | `enemy` | optional: whose town it is, 'enemy' or 'player' (default 'enemy'); only the other side's shot can sack it |

### `harbour`

A wharf with boats moored alongside and an anchorage off it (a ring of buoys). Your ships that lie still in the anchorage (anchored or barely moving) have their hulls patched by the yard’s carpenters, until its timber runs out. A harbour on a fort’s island serves whoever holds the fort. rate 0 makes it scenery.

| param | default | description |
|---|---|---|
| `r` | `75` | optional: anchorage radius in map units (default 75) |
| `rate` | `3` | optional: hull points a second for each ship in the anchorage (default 3; 0 = scenery) |
| `upTo` | `0.85` | optional: share of her full hull the carpenters can restore (default 0.85) |
| `stock` | `160` | optional: hull points of timber in the yard for the whole battle (default 160) |
| `team` | `player` | optional: whose ships it serves, 'player' or 'enemy' (default 'player'); a fort on its island overrides it |

### `lighthouse`

A striped lighthouse with a lamp that glows in fog and dusk; gulls circle it. Given sight, it lifts the fog around it for your lookouts: enemy ships within that range of it show (and can be shot at) wherever your fleet is.

| param | default | description |
|---|---|---|
| `sight` | `0` | optional: fog sight radius around it in map units, 0 = just a light (default 0) |

### `peak`

A high hill or mountain on an island or coast. High land steals the wind: in its lee (downwind of it, about 4 times its island's radius) ships sail slower, at worst 50% of the wind's speed right under it. Calm, glassy water shows where the lee lies, and it swings with the wind.

| param | default | description |
|---|---|---|
| `height` | `55` | optional: how high, in map units (default 55) |
| `size` | `0.75` | optional: how wide its foot is, as a share of the island radius (default 0.75) |
| `lee` | `4` | optional: how far its wind shadow reaches, in island radii (default 4; 0 = none) |
| `calm` | `0.5` | optional: share of the wind left right under it (default 0.5) |

### `volcano`

A peak with a smoking crater; like any peak it casts a lee downwind.

| param | default | description |
|---|---|---|
| `height` | `65` | optional: how high (default 65) |
| `size` | `0.65` | optional: foot as a share of the island radius (default 0.65) |
| `lee` | `4` | optional: wind shadow length in island radii (default 4) |
| `calm` | `0.5` | optional: wind left under it (default 0.5) |

### `church`

A church in the region’s style: an English chapel with a spire, or a whitewashed Spanish mission with a bell tower.

### `windmill`

A stone windmill whose sails turn in the wind.

### `ruin`

A crumbling stone temple overgrown with jungle: a stepped platform, broken columns and fallen blocks.

### `castle`

A honey-stone bastion on a headland in the style of El Morro, its walls angled to the sea, with a watchtower.

### `skull`

Skull Rock: a great white boulder with hollow eyes, staring out to sea.

### `wreck`

An old hull heeled over, ribs showing, on a beach, a reef or a shoal (ships can’t pass the land, and steer clear of the reef anyway). Gulls pick at it.

### `stacks`

Sea stacks: tall rock pillars with grassy tops standing in the surf at the shore, inside the land’s outline.

| param | default | description |
|---|---|---|
| `count` | `3` | optional: how many (default 3) |

### `mangroves`

A fringe of mangroves on their stilt roots along the shore, inside the land’s outline.

| param | default | description |
|---|---|---|
| `span` | `0` | optional: on an island, how many degrees of shore they cover; on a coast, how much of the edge (default 90 / 0.3) |

Example: Port Royal under siege, its harbour patching your ships while Spanish mortars set the town alight.

```js
siege: {
  style: 'port',
  landmarks: [
    { kind: 'town', island: 0, at: 150, d: 0.64, houses: 6, team: 'player', name: 'Port Royal' },
    { kind: 'harbour', island: 0, at: -60, r: 80 },
    { kind: 'lighthouse', island: 2, at: 0, d: 0.45 },
  ],
},
```

## Combat rules

From `RAKE` and `CRIT` in `src/sim/hazards.js`.

- **Raking fire.** A ball that flies within 22° of the target's bow-stern line has come in
  through her stern (×1.75 damage) or her bow (×1.5). The hit shows "Raked!" over the ship. Enemy captains
  come in at an angle rather than bows-on to a broadside, and some (bosses more often) work round to cross your stern
  while the broadside facing them is reloading.
- **Critical hits.** Each round-shot ball that lands (bow chasers too; not chain or grape) has a 3% chance
  of a lucky hit, 8% when it rakes (a stern rake finds the rudder twice as often):
  - *Mast down*: 30% slower for the rest of the battle (at worst 55% speed); she always keeps her main mast, and the lost one lies toppled over the side (`s.mastsDown`).
  - *Rudder shot away*: the helm answers at 50% for 8 s (`s.rudderT`).
  - *Fire aboard*: 2.4 hull a second for 5 s (`s.fireT`).
